claims.text: Cyclic or high-strain-rate loading at service-relevant temperatures will induce phase separation and nucleation of secondary phases in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Cyclic or high-strain-rate loading at service-relevant temperatures will cause dynamic strain aging and dislocation locking.
The load-induced microstructural instabilities will reduce toughness and promote brittle fracture.
The initial alloy is a uniform, single-phase solid solution without pre-existing secondary phases.
The unloaded as-synthesized baseline is fully ductile.
Elevated-temperature cyclic or high-strain-rate deformation represents demanding service conditions in aerospace, automotive, or fusion-reactor components.
Load-induced secondary-phase precipitation will occur particularly at grain boundaries.
Dynamic-strain-aging-related dislocation pinning will occur particularly at grain boundaries.
Applied mechanical stress increases local energy and mobilizes dislocations.
The stress-induced local conditions favor nucleation of brittle secondary phases.
The stress-induced local conditions enhance solute-dislocation interactions responsible for dynamic strain aging.
Secondary phases reduce stress redistribution and impede plastic deformation.
Dislocation locking reduces stress redistribution and impedes plastic deformation.
Loaded specimens will develop new diffraction peaks corresponding to secondary phases relative to thermally matched unloaded controls.
Loaded specimens will show TEM evidence of dislocation clusters or locking relative to unloaded controls.
The predicted phase or dislocation changes will correlate with reduced toughness and more brittle fracture behavior.
The extent and nature of microstructural evolution depend on alloy composition.
Thermally matched unloaded specimens provide the control for separating mechanical-loading effects from thermal effects.
The hypothesis is falsified if loading produces neither detectable secondary phases nor dislocation locking and toughness remains equivalent to the unloaded baseline.
